High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Krishna Mohan Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajendra Pratap Singh Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State .

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed praying for quashing the Criminal Case No. of 2023 (State Vs. Rahul and others) arising out of Case Crime No.151 of 2022 under Sections 498A,
323, 342, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kaimari, District Rampur, pending before the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (S.D), Rampur.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that vide order dated 22.11.2023 passed by this Court, the learned trial court was directed to verify the compromise deed dated 06.12.2023, entered between the parties.

entities.text: Criminal Case No. of 2023 (State Vs. Rahul and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In furtherance, to it, the compromise deed dated 06.12.2023 has been verified by the court concerned.
As per office report, in compliance of order dated 22.11.2023, a report from Learned Judicial Magistrate, Rampur is received and kept on record at Flag 'A'.

In view of the fact that the husband and wife do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them and as the matter is purely of personal nature and family dispute, which has been mutually settled between the parties in view of the compromise, which has also been verified by the concerned Court below, vide its report dated 07.12.2023, therefore, no useful purpose would be Rahul Bansal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160528510/
1 served in proceeding with the matter further.

entities.text: Rahul Bansal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana) as well as the Judgment of the Apex Court reported in J.T., 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another),
the entire proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby set aside.
